sanskrit: sa tu mām abravīd rājan mama pūrvaparigrahaḥ mṛgayādharmam utsṛjya kimarthaṃ tāḍitas tvayā
english: He then spoke to me, O king: 'This creature is my prior possession — abandoning the dharma of the hunt, why have you struck it?'

sanskrit: eṣa te niśitair bāṇair darpaṃ hanmi sthiro bhava sa varṣmavān mahākāyas tato mām abhyadhāvata
english: 'With my sharp arrows I shall destroy your pride — stand firm!' That great-bodied, towering figure then charged at me.

sanskrit: tato girim ivātyartham āvṛṇon māṃ mahāśaraiḥ taṃ cāhaṃ śaravarṣeṇa mahatā samavākiram
english: Then, like a mountain, he overwhelmed me with great arrows; and I in turn covered him with a mighty shower of shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarair dīptamukhaiḥ patritair anumantritaiḥ pratyavidhyam ahaṃ taṃ tu vajrair iva śiloccayam
english: Then I pierced him with blazing-tipped, feathered, and consecrated arrows, striking him as if with thunderbolts striking a mass of rocks.

sanskrit: tasya tac chatadhā rūpam abhavac ca sahasradhā tāni cāsya śarīrāṇi śarair aham atāḍayam
english: His form multiplied a hundredfold, then a thousandfold; and all those bodies of his I struck with my arrows.

sanskrit: punas tāni śarīrāṇi ekībhūtāni bhārata adṛśyanta mahārāja tāny ahaṃ vyadhamaṃ punaḥ
english: Again those bodies became one, O Bhārata, O great king, and again I shattered that single form.

sanskrit: aṇur bṛhacchirā bhūtvā bṛhac cāṇuśirāḥ punaḥ ekībhūtas tadā rājan so 'bhyavartata māṃ yudhi
english: He took a form tiny-bodied with enormous head, then enormous-bodied with a tiny head; then, made one again, O king, he came at me in battle.

sanskrit: yadābhibhavituṃ bāṇair naiva śaknomi taṃ raṇe tato 'ham astram ātiṣṭhaṃ vāyavyaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: When I could no longer overcome him in battle with arrows, I then invoked the wind-weapon, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: na cainam aśakaṃ hantuṃ tad adbhutam ivābhavat tasmin pratihate cāstre vismayo me mahān abhūt
english: Yet I could not slay him — it was as if a wonder had occurred. When that weapon too was repelled, great amazement overcame me.

sanskrit: bhūyaś caiva mahārāja saviśeṣam ahaṃ tataḥ astrapūgena mahatā raṇe bhūtam avākiram
english: And again, O great king, I then covered that being in battle with an even greater multitude of weapons.

sanskrit: sthūṇākarṇam ayojālaṃ śaravarṣaṃ śarolbaṇam śailāstram aśmavarṣaṃ ca samāsthāyāham abhyayām jagrāsa prahasaṃs tāni sarvāṇy astrāṇi me 'nagha
english: Invoking the Sthūṇākarṇa, the iron-net, the arrow-rain, the arrow-tempest, the mountain-weapon, and the stone-shower, I advanced — yet he swallowed all those weapons of mine, laughing, O sinless one.

sanskrit: teṣu sarveṣu śānteṣu brahmāstram aham ādiśam tataḥ prajvalitair bāṇaiḥ sarvataḥ sopacīyata upacīyamānaś ca mayā mahāstreṇa vyavardhata
english: When all those were spent, I invoked the Brahmā-weapon; thereupon blazing arrows gathered around him from all sides, yet as I pressed him with that great weapon, he only grew in power.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃtāpito loko matprasūtena tejasā kṣaṇena hi diśaḥ khaṃ ca sarvato 'bhividīpitam
english: Then the world was scorched by the radiance born from me; in an instant the quarters of the sky and the firmament blazed with light on all sides.

sanskrit: tad apy astraṃ mahātejāḥ kṣaṇenaiva vyaśātayat brahmāstre tu hate rājan bhayaṃ māṃ mahad āviśat
english: Even that weapon the great-radiant one shattered in an instant; and when the Brahmā-weapon was destroyed, O king, great fear entered into me.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ dhanur ādāya tathākṣayyau maheṣudhī sahasābhyahanaṃ bhūtaṃ tāny apy astrāṇy abhakṣayat
english: Then, taking up my bow with those two inexhaustible quivers, I struck the being at once with rapid blows — yet it devoured those weapons too.

sanskrit: hateṣv astreṣu sarveṣu bhakṣiteṣv āyudheṣu ca mama tasya ca bhūtasya bāhuyuddham avartata
english: When all weapons were spent and all arms devoured, between me and that being hand-to-hand combat ensued.

sanskrit: vyāyāmaṃ muṣṭibhiḥ kṛtvā talair api samāhatau apātayac ca tad bhūtaṃ niśceṣṭo hy agamaṃ mahīm
english: We grappled with fists and struck each other with open palms; but that being hurled me down, and I lay motionless on the ground.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasya tad bhūtaṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata saha strībhir mahārāja paśyato me 'dbhutopamam
english: Then that being, laughing, vanished on the spot together with the women, O great king, even as I watched — a sight beyond compare.

sanskrit: evaṃ kṛtvā sa bhagavāṃs tato 'nyad rūpam ātmanaḥ divyam eva mahārāja vasāno 'dbhutam ambaram
english: Having done all this, the blessed lord then assumed another form of his own — a divine form, O great king, clad in a wondrous garment.

sanskrit: hitvā kirātarūpaṃ ca bhagavāṃs tridaśeśvaraḥ svarūpaṃ divyam āsthāya tasthau tatra maheśvaraḥ
english: Abandoning the guise of the Kirata, the blessed lord, master of the thirty gods, assumed his own divine form and stood there — the great lord Maheśvara.

sanskrit: adṛśyata tataḥ sākṣād bhagavān govṛṣadhvajaḥ umāsahāyo haridṛg bahurūpaḥ pinākadhṛk
english: Then the blessed lord appeared in person — he whose banner bears the bull, companion of Umā, tawny-eyed, of many forms, bearer of the Pināka bow.

sanskrit: sa mām abhyetya samare tathaivābhimukhaṃ sthitam śūlapāṇir athovāca tuṣṭo 'smīti paraṃtapa
english: He approached me as I stood there facing him on the battlefield, and the trident-bearing lord said: 'I am pleased with you,' O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: tatas tad dhanur ādāya tūṇau cākṣayyasāyakau prādān mamaiva bhagavān varayasveti cābravīt
english: Then the blessed lord, taking up that bow along with the two quivers of inexhaustible arrows, gave them back to me and said: 'Choose a boon.'

sanskrit: tuṣṭo 'smi tava kaunteya brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te yat te manogataṃ vīra tad brūhi vitarāmy aham amaratvam apāhāya brūhi yat te manogatam
english: 'I am pleased with you, son of Kuntī; tell me, what shall I do for you? Whatever is in your heart, O hero, speak it — I shall grant it. Setting aside immortality, tell me what is in your mind.'

sanskrit: tataḥ prāñjalir evāham astreṣu gatamānasaḥ praṇamya śirasā śarvaṃ tato vacanam ādade
english: Then I, with joined palms, my mind fixed on weapons, bowed my head to Śarva and spoke these words.

sanskrit: bhagavān me prasannaś ced īpsito 'yaṃ varo mama astrāṇīcchāmy ahaṃ jñātuṃ yāni deveṣu kāni cit dadānīty eva bhagavān abravīt tryambakaś ca mām
english: 'If the blessed lord is pleased with me, this is the boon I desire: I wish to learn whatever weapons exist among the gods.' And the blessed Three-eyed Lord said to me: 'I shall give them.'

sanskrit: raudram astraṃ madīyaṃ tvām upasthāsyati pāṇḍava pradadau ca mama prītaḥ so 'straṃ pāśupataṃ prabhuḥ
english: 'The Raudra weapon, which is mine, will attend you, O Pāṇḍava.' And the gracious lord gladly bestowed upon me the Pāśupata weapon.

sanskrit: uvāca ca mahādevo dattvā me 'straṃ sanātanam na prayojyaṃ bhaved etan mānuṣeṣu kathaṃ cana
english: And Mahādeva said, having given me that ancient weapon: 'This must never be discharged against human beings under any circumstances.

sanskrit: pīḍyamānena balavat prayojyaṃ te dhanaṃjaya astrāṇāṃ pratighāte ca sarvathaiva prayojayeḥ
english: When you are severely pressed, Dhanañjaya, you may powerfully deploy it; and to counter enemy weapons you may always use it.

sanskrit: tad apratihataṃ divyaṃ sarvāstrapratiṣedhanam mūrtiman me sthitaṃ pārśve prasanne govṛṣadhvaje
english: That weapon, divine and irresistible, which nullifies all other weapons, stands beside me embodied, now that the bull-bannered lord is pleased.'

sanskrit: utsādanam amitrāṇāṃ parasenānikartanam durāsadaṃ duṣprahasaṃ suradānavarākṣasaiḥ
english: It is the annihilator of enemies, the destroyer of opposing armies, unapproachable and invincible to gods, demons, and rakshasas alike.

sanskrit: anujñātas tv ahaṃ tena tatraiva samupāviśam prekṣataś caiva me devas tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Given leave by him, I sat down right there, and as I watched, the god vanished in that very spot.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca tatas tām avasaṃ prīto rajanīṃ tatra bhārata prasādād devadevasya tryambakasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Arjuna said: Then, O Bhārata, I spent that night there in joy, by the grace of the god of gods, the great-souled Three-eyed Lord.

sanskrit: vyuṣito rajanīṃ cāhaṃ kṛtvā pūrvāhṇikakriyām apaśyaṃ taṃ dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ dṛṣṭavān asmi yaṃ purā
english: Having spent the night and performed my morning rites, I saw again that foremost of twice-born men whom I had seen before.

sanskrit: tasmai cāhaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ sarvam eva nyavedayam bhagavantaṃ mahādevaṃ sameto 'smīti bhārata
english: To him I reported everything that had occurred, exactly as it happened — that I had met the blessed Mahādeva himself, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa mām uvāca rājendra prīyamāṇo dvijottamaḥ dṛṣṭas tvayā mahādevo yathā nānyena kena cit
english: That best of twice-born men, filled with delight, said to me, O lord of kings: 'You have seen Mahādeva as none other has seen him.

sanskrit: sametya lokapālais tu sarvair vaivasvatādibhiḥ draṣṭāsy anagha devendraṃ sa ca te 'strāṇi dāsyati
english: Meeting with all the world-guardians, beginning with Vivasvat's son, you shall see Devendra, O sinless one, and he will give you weapons.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā sa māṃ rājann āśliṣya ca punaḥ punaḥ agacchat sa yathākāmaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ sūryasaṃnibhaḥ
english: Having said this, O king, that brahmin brilliant as the sun embraced me again and again, then departed as he wished.

sanskrit: athāparāhṇe tasyāhnaḥ prāvāt puṇyaḥ samīraṇaḥ punar navam imaṃ lokaṃ kurvann iva sapatnahan
english: Then in the afternoon of that same day a holy breeze arose, as if making the world new again, O slayer of enemies.

sanskrit: divyāni caiva mālyāni sugandhīni navāni ca śaiśirasya gireḥ pāde prādurāsan samīpataḥ
english: And divine, freshly fragrant garlands appeared at the foot of the Shaishira mountain, close at hand.

sanskrit: vāditrāṇi ca divyāni sughoṣāṇi samantataḥ stutayaś cendrasaṃyuktā aśrūyanta manoharāḥ
english: And on all sides were heard celestial instruments of fine resonance, and enchanting hymns of praise joined with Indra's name.

sanskrit: gaṇāś cāpsarasāṃ tatra gandharvāṇāṃ tathaiva ca purastād devadevasya jagur gītāni sarvaśaḥ
english: There, hosts of apsaras and gandharvas in front of the god of gods sang songs on every side.

sanskrit: marutāṃ ca gaṇās tatra devayānair upāgaman mahendrānucarā ye ca devasadmanivāsinaḥ
english: Hosts of Maruts arrived there in divine chariots — the attendants of Mahendra who dwell in the abode of the gods.

sanskrit: tato marutvān haribhir yuktair vāhaiḥ svalaṃkṛtaiḥ śacīsahāyas tatrāyāt saha sarvais tadāmaraiḥ
english: Then Marut's lord, drawn by bay steeds splendidly adorned, came there accompanied by Śacī and all the gods.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu kubero naravāhanaḥ darśayām āsa māṃ rājaṃl lakṣmyā paramayā yutaḥ
english: At that very moment, O king, Kubera, borne by men, revealed himself to me, adorned with supreme splendor.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi yamaṃ pratyapaśyaṃ vyavasthitam varuṇaṃ devarājaṃ ca yathāsthānam avasthitam
english: In the southern direction I beheld Yama stationed; I saw Varuṇa, the king of gods, established each in their proper place.

sanskrit: te mām ūcur mahārāja sāntvayitvā surarṣabhāḥ savyasācin samīkṣasva lokapālān avasthitān
english: Those bulls among gods spoke to me, O great king, soothing me: 'O Savyasācin, behold the world-guardians arrayed before you.'

sanskrit: surakāryārthasiddhyarthaṃ dṛṣṭavān asi śaṃkaram asmatto 'pi gṛhāṇa tvam astrāṇīti samantataḥ
english: 'You have seen Shankara for the accomplishment of the gods' purpose; now receive weapons from us as well, on every side.'

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ prayato bhūtvā praṇipatya surarṣabhān pratyagṛhṇaṃ tadāstrāṇi mahānti vidhivat prabho
english: Then, having purified myself and bowed to those bulls among gods, I duly received those great weapons, O lord.

sanskrit: gṛhītāstras tato devair anujñāto 'smi bhārata atha devā yayuḥ sarve yathāgatam ariṃdama
english: Having received the weapons, I was then dismissed by the gods, O Bhārata; and all the gods departed the way they had come, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: maghavān api deveśo ratham āruhya suprabham uvāca bhagavān vākyaṃ smayann iva surārihā
english: And Maghavan too, lord of gods, mounting his radiant chariot, spoke these words, the blessed slayer of the enemies of the gods, as if smiling.

sanskrit: puraivāgamanād asmād vedāhaṃ tvāṃ dhanaṃjaya ataḥ paraṃ tv ahaṃ vai tvāṃ darśaye bharatarṣabha
english: 'Before this coming of yours I already knew you, Dhanañjaya; henceforth I shall show myself to you further, O bull of the Bhāratas.'

sanskrit: tvayā hi tīrtheṣu purā samāplāvaḥ kṛto 'sakṛt tapaś cedaṃ purā taptaṃ svargaṃ gantāsi pāṇḍava
english: 'For you have bathed at the sacred fords again and again in former times, and this austerity you have now performed — you shall go to heaven, O Pāṇḍava.'

sanskrit: bhūyaś caiva tu taptavyaṃ tapaḥ paramadāruṇam uvāca bhagavān sarvaṃ tapasaś copapādanam
english: 'Yet still most severe austerity must be practiced'; and the blessed lord told me everything about the means of that austerity.

sanskrit: mātalir manniyogāt tvāṃ tridivaṃ prāpayiṣyati viditas tvaṃ hi devānām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca mahātmanām
english: 'Matali, by my command, shall bring you to the three heavens; for you are known to the gods and to the great-souled seers.'

sanskrit: tato 'ham abruvaṃ śakraṃ prasīda bhagavan mama ācāryaṃ varaye tvāham astrārthaṃ tridaśeśvara
english: Then I said to Śakra: 'Be gracious to me, O blessed lord; I choose you as my teacher for the purpose of learning weapons, O lord of the thirty gods.'

sanskrit: indra uvāca krūraṃ karmāstravit tāta kariṣyasi paraṃtapa yadartham astrāṇīpsus tvaṃ taṃ kāmaṃ pāṇḍavāpnuhi
english: Indra said: 'You will perform a cruel deed as a master of weapons, dear one, O scorcher of foes; whatever the purpose for which you desire those weapons — that wish, O Pāṇḍava, you shall attain.'

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca tato 'ham abruvaṃ nāhaṃ divyāny astrāṇi śatruhan mānuṣeṣu prayokṣyāmi vināstrapratighātanam
english: Arjuna said: Then I replied: 'I shall not discharge the divine weapons against human beings, O slayer of enemies, except to counter other weapons.'

sanskrit: tāni divyāni me 'strāṇi prayaccha vibudhādhipa lokāṃś cāstrajitān paścāl labheyaṃ surapuṃgava
english: 'Give me those divine weapons, O lord of the wise; and afterwards may I attain the worlds conquered by weapons, O best of gods.'

sanskrit: indra uvāca parīkṣārthaṃ mayaitat te vākyam uktaṃ dhanaṃjaya mamātmajasya vacanaṃ sūpapannam idaṃ tava
english: Indra said: 'This word was spoken to you by me only as a test, Dhanañjaya; your answer befits my own son — well spoken indeed.'

sanskrit: śikṣa me bhavanaṃ gatvā sarvāṇy astrāṇi bhārata vāyor agner vasubhyo 'tha varuṇāt samarudgaṇāt
english: 'Go to my abode and learn all weapons, O Bhārata — from Vāyu, from Agni, from the Vasus, from Varuṇa together with the hosts of Maruts.'

sanskrit: sādhyaṃ paitāmahaṃ caiva gandharvoragarakṣasām vaiṣṇavāni ca sarvāṇi nairṛtāni tathaiva ca madgatāni ca yānīha sarvāstrāṇi kurūdvaha
english: 'The Sadhya-weapon, the Pitāmaha-weapon, the weapons of the gandharvas, serpents, and rakshasas, all the Vaiṣṇava weapons, and likewise the Nairṛta weapons, and all weapons that abide with me here — learn them all, O chief of the Kurus.'

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca evam uktvā tu māṃ śakras tatraivāntaradhīyata athāpaśyaṃ hariyujaṃ ratham aindram upasthitam divyaṃ māyāmayaṃ puṇyaṃ yattaṃ mātalinā nṛpa
english: Arjuna said: Having thus spoken to me, Śakra vanished right there. Then I saw Indra's chariot yoked with bay steeds, divine, fashioned of illusion, sacred, made ready by Matali, O king.

sanskrit: lokapāleṣu yāteṣu mām uvācātha mātaliḥ draṣṭum icchati śakras tvāṃ devarājo mahādyute
english: When the world-guardians had departed, Matali then spoke to me: 'Śakra, the king of gods, wishes to see you, O greatly brilliant one.'

sanskrit: saṃsiddhas tvaṃ mahābāho kuru kāryam anuttamam paśya puṇyakṛtāṃ lokān saśarīro divaṃ vraja
english: 'You are accomplished, O mighty-armed one — perform this supreme purpose; behold the worlds of those who have done meritorious deeds and go to heaven in your very body.'

sanskrit: ity ukto 'haṃ mātalinā girim āmantrya śaiśiram pradakṣiṇam upāvṛtya samārohaṃ rathottamam
english: Thus addressed by Matali, I took leave of the Shaishira mountain, circumambulated it clockwise, and mounted that finest of chariots.

sanskrit: codayām āsa sa hayān manomārutaraṃhasaḥ mātalir hayaśāstrajño yathāvad bhūridakṣiṇaḥ
english: Matali, expert in the science of horses, skilled and expert, then drove the horses whose speed matched that of mind and wind.

sanskrit: avaikṣata ca me vaktraṃ sthitasyātha sa sārathiḥ tathā bhrānte rathe rājan vismitaś cedam abravīt
english: Then that charioteer glanced at my face as I stood there while the chariot sped along, O king, and amazed, he spoke these words.

sanskrit: atyadbhutam idaṃ me 'dya vicitraṃ pratibhāti mām yad āsthito rathaṃ divyaṃ padā na calito bhavān
english: 'What strikes me today as exceedingly wonderful and strange is that you have mounted this divine chariot and have not moved a step.'

sanskrit: devarājo 'pi hi mayā nityam atropalakṣitaḥ vicalan prathamotpāte hayānāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: 'For even the king of gods, as I have always observed here, sways at the first surge of the horses, O bull of the Bhāratas.'

sanskrit: tvaṃ punaḥ sthita evātra rathe bhrānte kurūdvaha atiśakram idaṃ sattvaṃ taveti pratibhāti me
english: 'But you remain perfectly steady here as the chariot races on, O foremost of the Kurus — your strength appears to me to surpass even Śakra's.'

sanskrit: ity uktvākāśam āviśya mātalir vibudhālayān darśayām āsa me rājan vimānāni ca bhārata
english: Having said this, Matali entered the sky and showed me, O king, the abodes of the gods and the celestial mansions, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nandanādīni devānāṃ vanāni bahulāny uta darśayām āsa me prītyā mātaliḥ śakrasārathiḥ
english: Matali, Śakra's charioteer, with affection showed me many forests of the gods — Nandana and others.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakrasya bhavanam apaśyam amarāvatīm divyaiḥ kāmaphalair vṛkṣai ratnaiś ca samalaṃkṛtām
english: Then I saw Śakra's abode, Amarāvatī, adorned with divine wish-fulfilling trees and with jewels throughout.

sanskrit: na tāṃ bhāsayate sūryo na śītoṣṇe na ca klamaḥ rajaḥ paṅko na ca tamas tatrāsti na jarā nṛpa
english: The sun does not light it — it shines with its own radiance; neither cold nor heat afflicts it, nor weariness; there is no dust, no mud, no darkness there, and no old age, O king.

sanskrit: na tatra śoko dainyaṃ vā vaivarṇyaṃ copalakṣyate divaukasāṃ mahārāja na ca glānir ariṃdama
english: No sorrow or destitution is seen there, no pallor, O great king, and no languor among the dwellers in heaven, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: na krodhalobhau tatrāstām aśubhaṃ ca viśāṃ pate nityatuṣṭāś ca hṛṣṭāś ca prāṇinaḥ suraveśmani
english: Neither anger nor greed exists there, nor anything inauspicious, O lord of the people; the living beings in the abode of the gods are ever contented and joyful.

sanskrit: nityapuṣpaphalās tatra pādapā haritacchadāḥ puṣkariṇyaś ca vividhāḥ padmasaugandhikāyutāḥ
english: The trees there always bear flowers and fruit with ever-green foliage, and there are various lotus-ponds filled with fragrant lotus blossoms.

sanskrit: śītas tatra vavau vāyuḥ sugandho jīvanaḥ śuciḥ sarvaratnavicitrā ca bhūmiḥ puṣpavibhūṣitā
english: A cool, fragrant, life-giving, and pure breeze blows there; and the ground is adorned with flowers and variegated with every kind of jewel.

sanskrit: mṛgadvijāś ca bahavo rucirā madhurasvarāḥ vimānayāyinaś cātra dṛśyante bahavo 'marāḥ
english: Many lovely deer and birds of sweet voice roam there, and many immortals are seen here moving about in celestial mansions.
